'''Kohaku Shrine''' (こはくじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine near {{ill|Jindai-ji (Tokyo)|Q500736|qid=Q500736}} in Sasu-cho, {{ill|Chōfu|ar|تشوفو (طوكيو)|azb|چوفو، توکیو|bg|Чофу|bn|চোফু, টোকিও|ca|Chōfu|ce|Тёфу|ceb|Chōfu-shi|cs|Čófu|de|Chōfu|el|Τσόφου (Τόκιο)|eo|Ĉofu (urbo)|es|Chōfu (Tokio)|et|Chōfu|eu|Chōfu|fa|چوفو، توکیو|fi|Chōfu|fr|Chōfu|gl|Chōfu, Tokyo|hy|Տյոֆու|id|Chōfu, Tōkyō|it|Chōfu|ja|調布市|ko|조후시|lt|Čiofu|mg|Chōfu|mn|Чоофү|ms|Chofu|mzn|چوفو، توکیو|nl|Chofu|no|Chofu|pl|Chōfu|pt|Chofu|ro|Chōfu|ru|Тёфу|sh|Chōfu|sr|Чофу|su|Chofu, Tokyo|sv|Chofu|tg|Чофу|th|โชฟุ|tl|Chōfu, Tokyo|tr|Chōfu|tt|Тёфу|tum|Chōfu|uk|Тьофу|ur|شؤفو، ٹوکیو|vi|Chōfu, Tokyo|war|Chōfu|zh|調布市|zh_classical|調布市|zh_min_nan|Tyôhu-chhī|zh_yue|調布市|qid=Q210667}}, {{ill|Tokyo|Q1490|qid=Q1490}}. It enshrines Otoshi Mioya no Kami. It is a candidate for the Engishiki shrine "Kohaku Shrine" of Tama District, Musashi Province, and was formerly ranked as a gosha and tutelary shrine of old Sasu Village.

=== History ===
According to shrine tradition, the shrine was founded in 588 by enshrining Otoshi Mioya no Kami. {{sfn|新編武蔵風土記稿 佐須村}}

Traditions connected with Jindaiji state that Manko Shonin's grandparents were worshiped here as guardian deities of Jindaiji.<ref name="jindaiji">''Jindaiji Engi''.</ref> The shrine name "Kohaku" is linked to stories about his grandmother "Tora" and grandfather "Ukon" and the old place-name "Komano-no-sato."<ref name="jindaiji"/>

In later centuries, Gion-ji (Kohakusan Nikko-in), founded by Manko Shonin, served as the shrine's betto temple until the Edo period.

; Shrine rank

=== Cultural properties ===
; Chofu City designated tangible cultural properties
* Honden (designated March 30, 2012)
: Built in 1683; repaired in 1815. One-bay nagare-zukuri mise-dana style. Original thatched roof replaced with copper sheeting.<ref name="cityprop">Chofu City Board of Education signboard for Kohaku Shrine Honden and three munafuda.</ref>
* Three munafuda attached to the honden (designated March 30, 2012)
: Include inscriptions from 750, 1683, and 1815.<ref name="cityprop"/>

; Other items
* Stone torii (built 1828)
* Monument "Komae-go Sasu-mura Kohaku Jinja no Hi"
* Komainu (built 1908)
* Haiden

=== Outside-precinct shrines ===
Sasu Shinmeigu and Kashinoki Inari, once merged in 1911, were re-enshrined at their former locations in 1942.<ref name="guide"/>

=== Annual events ===
* Monthly festival (13th of each month except January and October)
* New Year's Day festival (January 1)
* Inari Hatsuuma festival (first horse day of February)
* Kohaku Shrine grand festival (first Sunday of October)
* Shinmeigu grand festival (December 13)
* Niiname-sai (December 13)

=== Access ===
* From JR Mitaka Station, Keio Bus for Chofu Station; get off at "Sasu," about 5 minutes on foot.
* From Keio Chofu Station, Keio Bus for Mitaka Station; get off at "Sasu," about 5 minutes on foot.
* Chofu City minibuses also stop at "Kohaku Shrine."
